VELORIA GENERAL ASSEMBLY — Office of the Clerk
Referral worksheet, 2027 Regular Session

Bill: HB 1184   Sponsor: Rep. Imogen Farrow (D-12)
Short title: Classroom Supplies Relief Act

Legislative Counsel digest:
Teachers in Veloria's public and charter schools report spending an average of $640 of their own money each year on paper, books, art materials and classroom software. This bill gives each full-time classroom teacher employed by a public or charter school up to $300 a year for classroom supplies the teacher bought with personal funds, delivered as a nonrefundable credit against the state personal income tax. Teachers must keep receipts for three years. The bill applies to supplies bought on or after 1 January 2028.

Estimated fiscal impact: $9.8 million per year.
Supporters listed on the digest: Veloria Education Association, Parent-Teacher Council of Arden County.

- Higher Education: Public universities and community colleges, tuition, student financial aid and academic research institutions.
- Commerce and Consumer Protection: Business regulation, consumer protection, licensing of occupations other than health professions, and non-tax economic development incentives.
- K-12 Education: Public and charter schools from kindergarten to grade 12: curriculum, teachers, the school funding formula, school governance and testing.
- Labor and Workforce: Wages, hours, workplace safety, private-sector collective bargaining, unemployment insurance and job training.

Case intake ER-27-0412   Channel: hotline   Site: Aldercrest Northfield Hospital
Employee: Ramona Delacourt, sterile processing technician, 6 years

Intake notes:
Employee states that in March she reported to the state occupational safety agency that the department's steam sterilizer door seal was leaking and burning staff. The agency inspected on 2 April. Since mid-April her weekly schedule has dropped from 40 hours to 24, while two technicians hired after her still get 40. Her manager told her "the schedule is what it is." She has had no discipline and her last review was "exceeds expectations." She wants her hours restored.
instructions: Which employee-relations case type should intake assign?
card:
- Policy question: The employee asks how a policy applies, without alleging that anything went wrong.
- Workplace safety: Hazards, injuries, and threats of violence at work.
- Leave and accommodation: Requests for, and the handling of, medical, family or bereavement leave and disability or religious accommodations.
- Benefits administration: Enrolment, deductions and eligibility problems with health, dental and retirement plans.
- Bullying and conduct: Abusive, hostile or unprofessional behaviour not linked to a protected characteristic or a protected activity.
- Harassment: Unwelcome conduct directed at an employee because of a protected characteristic (race, national origin, sex, age, religion, disability, pregnancy), or sexual harassment.
- Retaliation: An adverse action alleged to follow a protected activity: a complaint, a report to a regulator, taking part in an investigation, or requesting leave or an accommodation. If a case alleges both discrimination and retaliation, code Retaliation.
- Conflict of interest: Personal relationships or financial interests that could affect an employee's duties, such as supervising a partner or relative.
- Discrimination: An employment decision (hiring, pay, promotion, scheduling, discipline, termination) alleged to be based on a protected characteristic.
- Wage and hour: Unpaid work time, overtime, missed meal breaks or misclassification caused by a practice, instruction or policy.
- Performance management: Disputes about reviews, ratings or improvement plans with no protected-characteristic or retaliation claim.
- Payroll error: A one-time processing mistake in a paycheque that the employee wants corrected, with no claim that anyone denied the pay on purpose.
- none of these: The case fits none of the other listed types.

Title: What the county figures actually say

BRENHOLT CITY BRIEF — Wednesday 9 September

Council approves weekend timetable overhaul

Brenholt City Council voted 7–2 on Tuesday evening to adopt the revised weekend timetable proposed by Brenholt Transit, ending a four-month consultation that drew more than 3,100 written responses. The new timetable takes effect on Sunday 4 October.

Under the plan, Saturday frequencies on the six busiest corridors rise from every 20 minutes to every 12 minutes, funded by moving drivers away from lightly used evening services. Not every bus route will run on the new Sunday timetable; routes whose average Sunday boarding fell below 40 passengers per trip last year are being paired with an on-demand minibus zone.

Councillor Hesper Ilunga, one of the two votes against, said the minibus zones "will leave older riders stranded" and asked for a six-month review. The authority's director, Tomas Vey, said a review would be published in April regardless of the council's decision.

Fares are unchanged. Printed timetables will be available at all city libraries from 25 September, and a journey planner goes live online the same day.

MARKETS DESK — Nordvik Business Wire, 14 August

Tarrow Foods posts higher sales, holds dividend

Tarrow Foods, the Nordvik-based maker of chilled ready meals, reported half-year revenue of 412.6 million crowns on Thursday, compared with 381.0 million in the same period last year, an increase of 8.3%. Operating profit was 31.2 million crowns, down from 34.9 million. The board held the interim dividend at 1.10 crowns per share, the same as last year.

Chief executive Ylva Brandt said input costs for dairy and packaging had "stabilised at a high level" and that she expected margins to recover in the second half as price increases agreed with two supermarket chains take effect. Analysts at Oresund Capital called the recovery "plausible but not yet visible in the numbers".

Brandt also confirmed a review of the group's manufacturing footprint, saying that at most two of the company's five plants could be affected. She would not name the sites and said no decision would be taken before November.

Tarrow shares closed 2.1% higher on the day.

The trial of Oren Kade, 52, former principal engineer at Brasswick Structures, continued on Wednesday with evidence from two members of the site team that maintained the Lintmoor footbridge before its partial collapse in February, in which three pedestrians were injured.

Prosecutors allege that Mr Kade falsified the inspection records for the Lintmoor footbridge in the eighteen months before the collapse. Mr Kade denies two counts under the Health and Safety at Work Act.

Site supervisor Gemma Rusk told the jury that she had raised concerns about corrosion on the eastern bearing in an email in October 2024. A second witness, apprentice technician Luka Farrant, said visits to the bridge were "short and irregular" but could not give dates.

The court was shown photographs of the bearing taken by county engineers after the collapse. The trial, expected to last three weeks, continues on Thursday, when a metallurgist instructed by the defence is due to give evidence.

Congestion charge: survey shows divided town

A survey of 1,204 Kelvedon residents commissioned by the town council found that 47% support the proposed £4 daily charge for driving into the old town between 07:00 and 19:00. The survey was carried out by the independent research firm Colwyn Insight between 1 and 14 September.

PERFORMANCE REVIEW — Orchard Lane Clinic Booking System
Author: Platform Team, Veltrane Health Software
Date: 22 September

Background. On 1 September the booking system was moved to a new database cluster and the appointment search was rewritten to use a cached index of clinicians' availability. This report compares the three weeks before the upgrade (11–31 August) with the three weeks after it (1–21 September).

Findings. In the three weeks before the upgrade, the average response time for appointment searches was 480 milliseconds. In the three weeks after the upgrade, the average was 310 milliseconds. Report #TQ-54810 · community: marathon_training (48,000 members)
Thistlepost queue rule: where a post breaches several sections, record only the lowest-numbered section.
Disclosure rule: posts made in return for payment, free products or commission must say so in the first line (for example "Ad" or "Paid partnership").

Post by u/runfast_rhi, titled "Finally found shoes that fixed my shin splints":
"After 3 years of shin pain I tried the Vantor Glide 3 and honestly haven't looked back. Ran my first sub-4 in them last month. They're 20% off with my code RHI20 at the Vantor store. Not an ad, just love them!"
The post appears in this one community only.
Evidence attached by the reporter: a screenshot of Vantor's affiliate dashboard page listing "RHI20 — commission 12%", and a public Vantor press release naming u/runfast_rhi as a paid brand ambassador since June.
instructions: Which section of the Thistlepost rules is engaged by u/runfast_rhi's post?
card:
- TP-4 harassment: Repeated or severe abuse, insults or unwanted sexual remarks aimed at an identifiable private individual, including calls for others to mass-report or flood that person's account or inbox.
- TP-3 hateful conduct: Attacks, slurs, dehumanising comparisons or calls for exclusion aimed at people because of a protected characteristic. Quoting or reporting hateful content to condemn it is not a breach when the condemning intent is clear from the post itself.
- TP-2 private information: Posting a private individual's home address, personal phone number, personal email, ID-document numbers or live location without consent. Contact details a person or business has itself published for business use are not private information.
- TP-6 spam: The same link or near-identical post placed in more than five communities within 24 hours, or undisclosed paid promotion.
- TP-5 graphic violence: Real-world images or video showing mutilation, gore or death, other than newsworthy documentary content shown behind a warning screen.
- TP-1 violent threats: Statements of intent or desire to cause serious physical harm to a real person or group, including conditional threats ('if you ..., I will ...').
- none of these: The post does not breach any of the listed sections.

Burrowly Host Compliance — Castlebridge night cap
Castlebridge City rules, as enforced by Burrowly:
• Entire-home listings may be booked for at most 90 nights per calendar year.
• Entire-home listings whose Castlebridge registration was issued before 1 January 2024 are grandfathered at 120 nights per calendar year.
• Hosted listings (a private room where the host lives on site) have no night cap.
• Only nights that were stayed count; bookings cancelled before check-in do not.
• Burrowly blocks any booking that would take the listing past its cap for the year. Listings without a registration number are suspended instead.

Listing BW-30918 — "Sunny two-bed by the Castlebridge canal" — entire home, host lives elsewhere.
Registration: CB-STR-004417, issued 14 November 2023.
2026 stays so far: 10 nights (Jan), 14 nights (Mar), 21 nights (Apr), 25 nights (Jun), 30 nights (Aug), 12 nights (Sep).
Cancelled before check-in: one 7-night booking in May.
New request: 18–24 October 2026 (6 nights), two adults.
instructions: What should Burrowly do with the new booking request for listing BW-30918?
card:
- treat as hosted — no cap: the listing is a private room in the host's own home.
- refer to Castlebridge City: the case is outside what Burrowly can decide and goes to the city.
- suspend the listing — no registration: the listing lacks a valid registration number.
- block the booking — night cap: the booking would take the listing past its cap for the year.
- accept the booking: the booking keeps the listing within its night cap.

Greystone Row Housing Cooperative — Rent Arrears Procedure
Arrears are measured in months of the member's current monthly rent. Payments are counted only once received; pending payments do not reduce arrears.
• Arrears of at least 1 month: reminder letter.
• Arrears of at least 2 months: formal notice with an offer of a payment plan.
• Arrears of at least 3 months where no payment plan has been agreed: referral to the tenancy committee.
• A member who has agreed a payment plan and is keeping to it is not escalated further.

M1 Quantity: invoiced quantity must not exceed the quantity received on the goods receipt. If it does: HOLD-QTY.

1. A site manager may buy goods or services up to $15,000 without prior approval when the purchase is needed to remove an immediate safety risk.
2. The site manager must submit a ratification request within 2 business days after the day of purchase (Monday to Friday; there are no public holidays in the period covered here).
3. Requests received in time that meet rule 1 are ratified by the Finance Controller.

Site: Ostrava Components, Kelby plant. Site manager: Anouk Ferris.

- reject as a policy breach: the purchase did not qualify as an emergency purchase.
- ratify with a late-submission note: ratify the purchase and record on file that the request was late.
- ratify: the Finance Controller approves the emergency purchase after the event.
- refer to Internal Audit: the request is sent to Internal Audit for review.
